title: Cooper Flagg: 34 Points as Dallas Erases a 21-Point Deficit
subheadline: Flagg scored 34 with eight assists, five steals and four blocks, and his late baskets sent Dallas into the NBA Cup knockout round for the first time.

body: Cooper Flagg carried the Dallas Mavericks back from 21 points down on Friday, Nov. 27, finishing with 34 points, seven rebounds, eight assists, five steals and four blocks in a 113-109 win at Phoenix.
His tip-in with 56 seconds left put Dallas ahead 107-106, and his turnaround jumper with under 24 seconds to go stretched the lead to three.
## Why fans are buying in

The win carried real weight. It finished a 4-0 run through NBA Cup group play, made Dallas the top seed in the West and put the franchise in the knockout round for the first time. It also stretched the Mavericks' winning streak to five games and lifted them to 12-7.

Flagg did it without Kyrie Irving or Dereck Lively II, who both sat out. In our analysis, that is what turns a young player into the face of a team: when the lineup thins out, the ball and the big moments keep finding him. A stat line that touches every column, from scoring to steals to blocks, is the kind fans notice long after the final buzzer.

He already has a published sales record to point to. Flagg ranked ninth on the NBA and NBPA's list of top-selling jerseys for the 2025-26 regular season, based on online sales at NBAStore.com and the Fanatics network, as a rookie.
## The look
Flagg wears No. 32. The banner above shows the blue Icon Edition, the white Association Edition and the navy Statement Edition, so a fan can pick the classic home blue or the darker alternate.
## Why this jersey will last

A second-year star who is not yet 20, on a team that keeps winning, gives this jersey years of runway. Next up is a Cup quarterfinal at home against San Antonio on Friday, Dec. 4, a national stage for another big night.

body: Scottie Barnes led the Toronto Raptors past the Brooklyn Nets 124-100 on Friday, Nov. 27, scoring 34 points on 11-of-20 shooting. He made all 10 of his free throws and added five assists and three blocks.
Immanuel Quickley backed him with a triple-double of 24 points, a season-high 14 assists and 10 rebounds.
## Why fans are buying in

Barnes has been Toronto's engine this fall, and this was a night when he did it efficiently: no wasted trips to the line, a strong mark from the floor and help at the rim on defense. The win lifted the Raptors to 7-11 and gave them a 3-1 finish in NBA Cup group play.

That record was good enough to hold the East wild-card spot until Atlanta's late win over Boston bumped Toronto out on point differential. In our analysis, that near miss says more about how close this group is than about where it stands, and Barnes is the player the whole build runs through.

He also checks the boxes fans look for in a long-term jersey. He is a homegrown pick who has spent his whole career in Toronto, he plays both ends, and he is the name Raptors fans across Canada already know. For a team building around youth, he is the obvious choice for the back of a shirt.
## The look

Barnes wears No. 4. The banner above shows the red Icon Edition and the black Statement Edition. The red is the brighter home look, while the black is a sleek option that works well away from the arena.
## Why this jersey will last

A franchise forward in his prime, on a young roster that keeps getting closer, gives this jersey staying power. Toronto hosts Denver on Sunday, Nov. 29, a chance to keep the run going against a contender.

title: T.J. Watt: Black Friday Touchdown in 27-5 Rout of Denver
subheadline: Watt fell on a Bo Nix fumble in the end zone for the game's first points as Pittsburgh's defense scored twice before halftime and ended Denver's six-game win streak.
description: T.J. Watt recovered a fumble in the end zone for the first score as the Steelers beat Denver 27-5 on Black Friday, ending a six-game streak. Why No. 90 fits.
primaryKeyword: T.J. Watt touchdown Broncos Black Friday
searchIntent: Steelers fans who watched the Black Friday rout want what Watt did and the right No. 90 jersey.
body: T.J. Watt put the first points on the board in Pittsburgh's 27-5 win over the Denver Broncos on Black Friday, Nov. 27, at Acrisure Stadium. With Watt and Nick Herbig closing in, the ball came loose from Bo Nix on Denver's second possession, and Watt fell on it in the end zone for a touchdown.
## Why fans are buying in

That play set the tone for one of the Steelers' best defensive nights in years. Jalen Ramsey added a 36-yard interception return for a score, and Pittsburgh became the first Steelers team since 1995 to return two takeaways for touchdowns in the first half. Denver finished with just 205 yards, and its six-game winning streak was over.

The result moved Pittsburgh to 7-4 and kept it perfect at home at 5-0. It also produced a final score that had never happened in NFL history. In our analysis, a national-TV rout of a team that came in at 8-2 is the kind of game that reminds the whole league who leads this defense, and Watt is still the name at the center of it.

His merchandise has a long, published track record. Watt ranked 15th on the NFLPA's Top 50 player sales list for March 1, 2025 to Feb. 28, 2026, after ranking 16th the year before. The NFLPA list counts all licensed player merchandise, led by jerseys.
## The look

Watt wears No. 90. The banner above shows the black home jersey, the white road version and the black alternate, plus this season's Salute to Service style, so there is a look for game day and for the stands.
## Why this jersey will last

Few defenders have been the face of a franchise as long as Watt has in Pittsburgh, and a 7-4 team in the playoff chase gives fans more reasons to wear his number. The Steelers host Houston in prime time on Sunday, Dec. 6.
